name: Solver Creator
tagline: Turn what you know into a complete, valid Solver, step by step
description: The platform's free Solver that guides anyone to build an excellent Solver package with their own AI (Claude Code, Claude or ChatGPT). In 7 steps it helps you define the promise and the audience, choose the differentiators, write the process with checklists, organize knowledge with source and date, plan the first-use calibration and build the test cases. Along the way it queries the server validator, which points out each error and how to fix it, and at the end it hands you the ZIP ready to publish through the site, where a team member reviews it within 5 business days. It does not write your knowledge for you, does not promise a rating or approval, and does not accept Finance, Legal or health packages in this phase.

creator.name: Solvers
creator.bio: The Solvers platform team. It maintains the package format, the validator and the review of published Solvers.

packageContents: A 7-step method, from the promise to a ready ZIP, with a checklist in each step
A package validator that points out each error, its path and how to fix it
A knowledge base with the package format, the error codes and best practices by type of Solver
Two complete example packages, a minimal one and a richer one
Ready-made templates: manifest, step, knowledge, test case, calibration, reviewer README and submission checklist
Memory of your level and of the type of Solver you want to create, between sessions

steps.title: Promise and audience
gate: Creator profile checked and used to adjust the level of the conversation
Promise in one sentence (what it solves and for whom) approved by the user
At least 3 items that the Solver does NOT do defined
Category chosen among those allowed to new creators (no Finance, Legal or health)
tagline, description and at least 8 searchPhrases drafted within the limits

steps.title: Differentiators and how to prove them
gate: At least 2 differentiators chosen among memory, liveData and escalation
For each differentiator, the proof the reviewer will check is written down
The user understood that tools and automatic verification are left for the Opening phase
If escalation: the user confirmed they will respond and will link Telegram on their profile
If liveData: who updates it, how often, and the review date defined

steps.title: Process and gates
gate: 3 to 6 steps defined, each with a goal and a verifiable output
Each step file has the 5 sections and between 400 and 12,000 characters
Each step has 3 to 6 objective gate items
If memory was chosen, at least one step mentions and uses the user's profile
validate_package run with no errors in the steps and the manifest

steps.title: Knowledge with source, date and rights
gate: Sources listed and rights of use confirmed by the user
Each .md file has front-matter with source and source_date (YYYY-MM-DD)
PDFs, pages and spreadsheets converted into .md by headings, with sections of 200 to 2,000 characters
Content that expires has valid_until
No personal data, passwords or text copied without permission
Sizes within the limits: file up to 10 MB and ZIP up to 50 MB

steps.title: Tools and verification
gate: The user understood that, in the Core phase, the package carries no tools, verifier or guarantee
Plan for future tools recorded (name, input, output and reason) or the word none
Substitute verification defined: objective gates, templates and test cases
Manifest without tools and with guarantee.available equal to false

steps.title: Calibration and memory
gate: 1 to 5 calibration questions with id, ask, why and, if closed, 2 to 6 options
No question asks for sensitive data
What becomes the profile (a lasting preference) separated from what stays out; notes only on the user's request
Steps adjusted to use the profile and usesMemory equal to true in the manifest
Behavior for someone who skips the questions defined

steps.title: Test cases and ready ZIP
gate: 10 or more test cases (target: 12) with checks that really test something
validate_package with no errors, and the remaining warnings justified
ZIP with 1 root folder containing manifest.json, only .json, .md and .txt, no system junk
Whole-ZIP validation done (script) or the user knows the site validates again on submission
Reviewer README.md and pre-submission checklist filled in
The user knows that submission is at /creator/publish and that human review takes up to 5 business days

tools.name: validate_package
tools.description: Validates the manifest and the steps of a Solver package with the rules for new creators (specVersion 1). Input: manifest (the manifest.json as an object), steps (a list of { file, content } with the text of each step) and, optionally, files (a list of { path, size } with all the package's files), knowledge (a list of { path, head } with the first lines of each knowledge file), templates (a list of { path, content }) and evals (a list of { path, content }). Output: ok, errors and warnings (each with code, path, message and fix), stats and summary. Use it in steps 3 and 7. It does not validate the whole ZIP: that happens in the script and on submission through the site.

beforeAfter.prompt: I want to create a Solver about closing the month for a Brazilian MEI (micro-entrepreneur) and sell it. How do I do it?
beforeAfter.withoutSolver: Great idea! Write a really detailed prompt explaining the MEI rules, ask the AI to act as an accountant and publish it somewhere. Tip: put effort into the instructions and test with a few examples.
beforeAfter.withSolver: Before any text, the promise: what does your Solver solve and for whom? I propose: 'close the month for a Brazilian MEI without mistakes: limit, DAS (the monthly tax slip) and report'. Then we choose at least 2 differentiators the reviewer can check (for example, a knowledge base with source and date for the DAS values and a calibration that asks the MEI's activity). Next we write 3 steps with a checklist, the knowledge base with source and source_date, 10 test cases and run the validator, which points out each error and how to fix it. At the end you get the ZIP ready to publish; a team member reviews it within 5 business days. Since the content is tax-related, it needs a clear reminder to check the official portal. Do you already have the material (laws, tables, notes) or do we start collecting it?

beforeAfter.prompt: I have a 60-page PDF with my method. Can I upload it as it is?
beforeAfter.withoutSolver: You can try uploading the PDF. If there is a problem, convert it to another format.
beforeAfter.withSolver: Not yet: in this phase the package only accepts .md and .txt (PDF comes later). I convert the PDF here, in your AI, into short .md files split by headings, each with source (where it came from), source_date (the date of the source) and, if it expires, valid_until. First, confirm that you have the right to use the content: third-party material without permission does not pass review. Want to start with the 3 most important chapters and then keep going?

versions.notes: English becomes the primary language: method, knowledge base and templates were translated, and the Portuguese storefront text moved to locales/pt.json. The AI still answers in the user's language.
First version: a 7-step method, a package validator, a knowledge base with the format, error codes, best practices and two complete examples, and ready-made templates.
